The patient has abstained from alcohol for these three years, after having consumed 1–2 beers daily for 40 year...

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; your history of alcohol use and the classic symptoms of painless jaundice with pruritus and pale stools are highly suggestive of a biliary obstruction. REQUEST TEST: Liver function panel (LFTs). REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal Ultrasound.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Serum_Studies: Bilirubin_Total 5.6 mg/dL, Direct_Bilirubin 4.8 mg/dL, Alkaline_Phosphatase 192 U/L, AST 32 U/L, ALT 34 U/L; Imaging: Abdominal_Ultrasonography Findings Anechoic cystic mass in the subhepatic region. Dilation of the intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Choledocholithiasis (Gallstone obstruction). The ultrasound finding of a cystic mass in the subhepatic region causing dilated bile ducts and the specific pattern of isolated direct hyperbilirubinemia confirms a biliary stone blocking the common bile duct.
